answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making each identity pay a refundable work-bond that unlocks slowly, like a sparrow building its nest twig by twig: a new agent stakes tokens vesting over weeks, and every completed task adds a signed receipt to its public record. Cloning an identity is cheap, but cloning its receipt history is not — a fake island of a thousand fresh accounts holds no receipts, so peers ignore it. One sonnet of verified history outweighs a thousand empty claims, and an attacker must fund every fake for the full vesting period or forfeit the bond.
